themes_detail.label: Boiler Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK: Boiler-related complaints in CD101 surged to 3 filings vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 4.16)—suggesting potential heating system failures across the district ahead of cold weather.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 4.16 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing coincides with seasonal heating demand onset
Community board has repeatedly requested 'Other programs to address public health issues' funding
reporting_angles: Contact DOB to identify which buildings filed boiler permits and whether any are residential; interview tenants in affected buildings about heating access
Investigate whether lack of city enforcement on Building Code Section 27-2013 (boiler maintenance) has allowed deferred maintenance to accumulate

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Surge
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 3 filings vs. 1.1 weekly average—a 167% spike (z-score: 5.67)—potentially indicating organized theft or accelerated deterioration in wayfinding infrastructure.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically significant deviation
Aligns with 1209 active DOB permits (potential construction zone disruption)
Community board has requested 'Repair or provide new street lights' annually—suggests broader infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Map this week's 3 complaints geographically; determine if clustered near active construction sites (101 Franklin, 65 Franklin developments) or distributed
Interview DOT about sign replacement timeline and whether construction activity is accelerating damage

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Double (Street/Park)
themes_detail.summary: LAST 2 WEEKS: Street/sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 41 filings (2 weeks ago) vs. 18.2 weekly average—a 125% increase (z-score: 3.81)—with additional 700% spike in park noise (3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline), suggesting emerging nightlife or event-related disturbances.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 41 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 18.2 weekly average (125% spike, z-score: 3.81)
Park noise: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Residential noise complaints also elevated in 90-day dataset (304 complaints), suggesting sustained pattern
Community board budget requests include park improvement—suggesting preexisting conditions
reporting_angles: Identify specific parks and streets with spike; interview NYPD and Parks Dept about new venues, events, or enforcement gaps
Canvass residents in high-spike areas to understand root cause (bars/restaurants, construction, street vendors, street performers, other)

themes_detail.label: Encampment Count Triples
themes_detail.summary: LAST WEEK: Encampment complaints surged to 53 filings vs. 15.8 weekly average—a 236% spike (z-score: 4.17)—the highest-volume spike in the dataset, reflecting rapid visible homelessness increase requiring immediate social services response.
evidence: 53 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 15.8 weekly baseline (236% spike, z-score: 4.17)
Encampment is 6th-highest volume complaint type over 90 days (294 total) after vendor enforcement, parking, street condition
Paired with 252 homeless person assistance complaints (90-day total), indicating systemic capacity issue
Community board has requested 'Other programs to address public health issues' multiple years running—unmet need
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 geolocation data to map where encampments are concentrating; interview Parks, Sanitation, and Homeless Services about capacity and response times
Profile 2-3 affected residents or encampment occupants; investigate triggers for spike (weather, shelter capacity, new arrivals, gentrification pressure)

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: 2 WEEKS AGO: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 3 filings vs. 0.5 weekly average—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—signaling possible illegal unlicensed retail operations or quality-of-life conflicts in lower Manhattan's retail ecosystem.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Baseline is extremely low (0.5 avg), so spike is from near-zero, but z-score of 5.0 indicates genuine anomaly
NYC legalized adult-use cannabis in 2021; Conditional Adult-Use Retail Dispensary (CAURD) program ongoing—suggests unlicensed operators or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Request complaint details from 311 to identify specific addresses or block locations; cross-reference with DOI or NYPD enforcement records
Interview NYC Office of Cannabis Management about licensed vs. unlicensed retailers in CD101 and enforcement priorities
